Done. I stopped at D1, as the brief's gate requires. Committed as `7c1b1ba` on `feat/progress-and-joinall`. Nothing in `desk/` changed.

## What I measured before

Pier `~bus` at `~/piers/joinall-bus`, port 8092, Vere 4.6. Running source confirmed by scry first (`lib/git-delta/hoon`, 2,988 bytes, `next-output` at offset 2,536 — the pairwise form). All timings from `~> %bout` in the pier log; all outputs checked against a Python reference by SHA-1.

**The brief's byte counts reproduce exactly** — 8,995 objects, 6,222 deltified, worst object 1,264 instructions / 247,348 bytes, 5,167,766,168 bytes copied whole-pack against 189,947,130 linear.

**The exponent does not.** On prefixes of erpit's worst real delta stream:

| instructions | bytes copied | ms |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 158 | 4,041,438 | 2.007 |
| 316 | 16,075,599 | 4.259 |
| 632 | 50,198,771 | 9.110 |
| 1,264 | 162,597,787 | 19.470 |

**Fitted exponent 1.09.** Bytes copied grow 40×; time grows 9.7×. Three real objects copying 11.1 / 12.7 / 13.5 MB take 1.17 / 2.23 / 4.65 ms — time tracks instruction count, not bytes.

A controlled run (1,264 instructions fixed, chunk size varied) isolates it: 156 M extra bytes copied costs 3.8 ms, i.e. 41 GB/s. erpit's accumulator maxes at 247 KB, stays in cache, and the median deltified object has **5 instructions**. The dominant term is ~19 µs of interpreted per-instruction work.

## What I measured after

I built the D2 rewrite **on the pier only** so the report could state its value rather than guess. Byte-identical on all 17 fixtures and on the whole 9,048-object pack (`mug 0x7b1d6883` both ways).

- Whole-pack `decode-pack-with`: **2.459 s → 2.416 s (1.8%)**
- Above 1 MB the defect is real: exponent **1.83 → 1.01**, a 20 MB object **687 ms → 26 ms (26.8×)**

That 1.8% on the workload the brief names, plus the 1.09 exponent, is why I stopped.

## What I changed

Only `QUESTIONS.md`. It carries the raw timings, the guard-equivalence argument, the byte-identity table, and four options with what each breaks.

## Call sites audited (D4, all nine)

Four accumulator loops: `git-delta.hoon:78`, `:85`; `git-inflate.hoon:265`; `urgit.hoon:3514` (peer assembly — bounded at 64 fragments × 1 MiB = ~2.1 GB copied worst case; owned by the parallel task, untouched). Four one-shot: `git-archive.hoon:119`, `git-pack.hoon:100`, `git-protocol.hoon:306`, `git-codec.hoon:100`. One false positive: `docket.hoon:118` is `+join` over a `(list tape)`.

**D3 confirmed and worse than stated.** `copy-distance` reads back from its own accumulator at `:206`. The brief treats `inflate-deflate:265` as separately fixable — it is not: that `output` flows into `compressed-block` at `:280` and then into `copy-distance` at `:237`. One accumulator, shared across block types.

## Left undone

D5, D6, D7 — not reached. Two unrelated defects found while measuring, both recorded: a push updating **more than one ref** returns 400 (`parse-receive-command`, `git-protocol.hoon:176-189`), and any push over `http.postBuffer` returns 400 because git sends a flush-only probe first (`urgit.hoon:7996`). Together they blocked the full-repository external push; a single-ref push of erpit's `master` (3.89 MB) runs in 1.90 s. The brief's reference file `click-probe-syntax-and-timing.md` does not exist in this repository.

The prototype is left at `~/piers/joinall-bus/urgit/lib/ad-proto.hoon` with the fixtures under `dat/`. I stopped only the pier I started, by the PID bound to 8092, verified as the `joinall-bus` process; 8080–8084 and 8090 are still up.
